The amplitude $ a $ is the distance from the midline (which is $ y = 1 $) to the maximum or minimum value. The amplitude is $ 3 - 1 = 2 $, so $ a = 2 $. The period of the function is the horizontal distance between two consecutive peaks or troughs. From the graph, the period is $  rac{2\pi}{3} $, so $ b = 3 $. The phase shift is the horizontal shift of the graph from the origin. The graph is shifted to the left by $  rac{\pi}{3} $, so the phase shift is $ - rac{\pi}{3} $. The phase shift is given by $ - rac{c}{b} $, so $ - rac{c}{3} = - rac{\pi}{3} $, which implies $ c = \pi $.
